project.name: NakedPak
project.subtitle: US consumer brand, name to come
project.intro: Name, visual identity and master outer box for a DTC soup and stew launch. Chef-crafted broths in a seaweed pouch that dissolves in boiling water in two minutes. Food first, magic second.

brief.label: Assignment
brief.headline: Name, identity and master box for the US direct-to-consumer launch.
brief.body: Create the consumer brand name, visual identity and master outer-box packaging for the DTC soup and stew launch (late March). “NakedPak” is the B2B seaweed-film name; “Deserved” was an investor placeholder.
list: Master outer box for 1 hero SKU, 6 dissolvable pouches per box, built on FPO dimensions and panels

brief.label: Opportunity
brief.headline: Culinary comfort without plastic or prep.
brief.body: Chef-crafted bone-broth and plant-based soups. The seaweed pouch dissolves in boiling water in two minutes, thickening the broth with zero waste and zero plastic contact. Proving people love the “drop, cook, dissolve” ritual in DTC creates a category of one and unlocks B2B food partners.

brief.label: Audience
brief.headline: Busy households and working professionals.
brief.body: Want a nourishing, cozy meal in minutes without giving up flavor, clean ingredients or easy prep. Secondary: campers, travelers and students who want lightweight, packable real meals with zero trash left behind.

brief.label: Tension
brief.headline: Effortless, waste-free comfort food, but “eating the wrapper” sounds like a science experiment.
brief.body: Lead with tech and shoppers hesitate. Hide the pouch and they miss the magic of the one-step ritual.

brief.label: Lens
brief.headline: Food first, magic second.
brief.body: Sell the steaming bowl and chef-crafted broth before explaining the film. Frame the seaweed pouch as natural as an apple or tomato skin: part of the recipe that locks in flavor and melts into the broth.

brief.label: Desired response
brief.quote: That looks delicious. Wait, I just drop the whole pouch in boiling water and it melts into the broth? I want to try that.
brief.body: Craving before curiosity. Warm, culinary, effortless and naturally smart; never clinical or gimmicky.

brief.label: Naming
brief.headline: Culinary warmth, nourishment or the effortless ritual, not packaging tech.
brief.body: Warm, appetizing and extensible beyond soup: ramen, oats, sauces.

brief.label: Box hierarchy
brief.headline: Read in three seconds.
steps: Appetizing, food-first brand and flavor call

brief.label: Identity and packaging
brief.headline: A rich, tactile culinary world on the outer cardboard box.
brief.body: 6 pouches inside; the inner pouch is unprinted clear film. Custom iconography makes the 3-step prep unmistakable at a glance. Flavor system: master architecture for 1 hero SKU that flexes across bone-broth and vegan/legume varieties.

brief.label: Guardrails
brief.headline: The work should not:
list: Lead with “edible packaging” or lab-tech language that makes the meal feel synthetic or experimental
Look like eco-austerity (beige craft-paper clichés) or cheap college instant noodles
Overcomplicate the prep story; the ritual must read in three seconds
Wait on final recipes or exact box dimensions; build on FPO dimensions and nutrition panels to hit Dec 18

entries.title: A Pinch Of
entries.tagline: SKINN case study: ready-to-heat meals renamed and repackaged.
entries.note: Nice case study elements and formatting.
entries.relevance: Same shelf problem as ours: a ready-to-heat meal line renamed, re-voiced and repackaged to win the fridge aisle. Scope maps almost one-to-one: naming, verbal identity, visual identity, packaging, imagery.

elements.label: Opener
elements.text: Name, an em dash, then a one-line repositioning: “A Pinch Of — Redefining ready-to-heat meals.” Set at text size above the hero, not as a giant headline.

elements.label: Side panel
elements.text: Sticky accordion beside the images: Expertise tags, then Challenge, Strategy, Branding, Imagery. Each is a small label plus a one-line headline that opens to prose. Branding splits into Naming, Verbal identity, Visual identity.

elements.label: Before / after
elements.text: Old and new pack shot top-down on white with a soft shadow, tiny uppercase captions. The fastest proof of the work.

elements.label: Image rhythm
elements.text: One column of full-width frames alternating with 2-up pairs and a solid color plate carrying only the logotype; pack-in-context, hand-held stack, fridge, social posts.

elements.label: Related cases
elements.text: Four-up cards: bold “Name — tagline.” running straight into a gray description.

elements.label: Type
elements.text: One neutral grotesk (Suisse Int’l) for every line of site text; the serif logotype is the only brand voice on the page.
